LLM auditresponse for update.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `update.sh` script is a maintainer helper script designed to automate version and checksum updates in the PKGBUILD by fetching the latest release information from the official upstream manifest at `https://dl.sanalyer.com/desktop/stable/linux/x64/latest.json`. It uses `curl` to retrieve the manifest and `jq` to extract the version and SHA-256 checksum of the tarball, then updates the `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, and `sha256sums` fields in the PKGBUILD accordingly.

The script operates only on local packaging files (PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO) and performs no file modifications, system changes, or network operations beyond updating metadata from a trusted, package-related domain. The domain `dl.sanalyer.com` appears to be the official distribution point for the software, and retrieving version and hash information from there is consistent with standard AUR maintenance practices. There is no use of `eval`, no execution of downloaded code, and no exfiltration of data.

While the script does not pin to a specific commit or use a cryptographic signature to verify the manifest, this is a common limitation of automated bump scripts and falls under maintainability rather than a security vulnerability. The operations are transparent, and the script does not introduce malicious behavior. Therefore, it is deemed SAFE.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Maintainer script safely updates version and hash from official source</summary>
</security_assessment>
